newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's new chancellor breaks silence...just.
newsitem.headline: Austria's new chancellor breaks silence...just.

text.p: Austrian chancellor-designate Viktor Klima broke his silence on Monday for the first time since the resignation of chancellor Franz Vranitzky but only to say he did not want to make any comment yet.
Austrian news agency APA managed to contact Klima briefly after he has lain low since Vranitzky announced his resignation after nearly 11 years in power on Saturday.
Klima, 49, who Vranitzky said had been reluctant to take over the top job, told APA he was only entitled to make any comment on his current duties. He is still technically finance minister.
President Thomas Klestil asked Vranitzky to stay on as acting chancellor until Klima had been officially sworn in, probably some time later this week.
But Klima's silence has surprised the Austrian and foreign media, who expected him at least to acknowledge publicly his promotion to Austria's eighth chancellor since 1945.
"I will only speak once I am officially chancellor," Klima said, asking for the public's understanding.
